scope: Independent local source review only; no remote load, no performance claim, and no change to frozen F.
result: No concrete remaining source blocker found after b1180f72 restores the multi-result release boundary.

resolved_finding.initial_behavior: Changing consuming Vec iteration to ids.iter kept Many(Vec) alive across the final filtered-name lookup, unlike the old IntoIter release at loop end.
resolved_finding.fix: Explicit drop(ids) immediately after the final consuming loop, before written handling and any later lookup.

reviewed_invariants.finding: Empty/One/Many owns only copied EntryId handles or the original Vec. The slice reference belongs to the result enum, not cache storage; no Arc or index reference is retained. Cache::get still verifies slot generation on every use.

The usable singleton branch still calls the same invalid(slot, now) before kind matching, including stale-policy expiry and invalid CNAME targets. It invokes the same remove path before returning Empty; unsupported kinds return Empty without promotion.

A matching singleton still unlinks and links the same slot at the LRU head, then returns the current ID. A singleton cannot require round-robin rotation. The ordinary multi-slot lookup and its snapshot drop, rotate_matches and final reverse are unchanged.

Question pointer, owner address, root allocation pointer, name revision and saturated revision checks are unchanged. Insertion/removal/clear/rotation invalidate through existing revision updates; failed generation checks fall back to the ordinary lookup.

DO and filtered/NXDOMAIN paths may reuse the hint. Mismatching-kind lookup keeps a still-valid hint; promotion does not change membership; expiry/removal changes revision so the next call falls back. No new result state is used as a future hint.

All first/is_empty/len/iter consumers access the same ordered slice. Empty stays empty; One has exactly the same ID; Many wraps the exact ordinary Vec, including zero-length or singleton fallback results. Three loop syntax changes copy IDs without changing order or filtering.
Result storage introduces no new copy-on-write ownership. Cache snapshots retain their existing separate mutable links/index behavior; Many continues to use the ordinary lookup implementation.

The final explicit drop restores the original multi-result free point. Early-return paths drop the result while returning as before. Public lookup/lookup_question continue returning Vec; only crate-internal hinted lookup changes representation.

controls_read_not_rerun: New 0/1/3 record comparison across lower/mixed case, time100/160, round-robin on/off and requested IPv4/IPv6; checks IDs, LRU endpoints, revision, subsequent order and original snapshot invariance.
Existing missing/added member, changed question, cache replacement/move, saturated revision, unique-many Arc/COW and mixed-RR rotation controls.
limits: Root reports 63 cache controls passed and one pre-existing ignored control; this review did not independently rerun them.
Root allocation probes are separate artifacts; no full CPU/timing claim is inferred.
A future candidate still needs complete allocation/fault, full correctness and unchanged performance/resource acceptance.
This prototype is separate from F3a3d8e3e, whose full qualification remains underway.
